https://oceea.osce.org/event/667089.text: Skip Links Skip to content Skip to main navigation Skip to search Home About us Our work News Events Resources Home About us Our work News Events Resources Joint Preparatory Meeting of the 32nd OSCE Economic and Environmental Forum Conference Date: 7 - 8 September 2026 Location: Hofburg, Vienna, Austria Organized by: Office of the Co-ordinator of OSCE Economic and Environmental Activities, under the guidance of Malta’s OSCE Chairpersonship 2024 Series: Economic and Environ­mental Forum Source: Office of the Co-ordinator of OSCE Economic and Environmental Activities , OSCE Chairpersonship The Joint Preparatory Meeting of the 32nd OSCE Economic and Environmental Forum dedicated to “Strengthening security and stability in the OSCE area through anticipating technologies and science-based diplomacy” will take place at the Hofburg premises, in Vienna, on 7 and 8 September 2026. The Economic and Environmental Forum is the main meeting-cycle within the Economic and Environmental Dimension of the OSCE. Its objectives are to identify needs and priorities, to raise awareness and to stimulate the political will of the 57 OSCE participating States in dealing with economic, environmental and security related challenges, to share best practices, as well as to provide a platform for dialogue with representatives of International Organizations, the business and academic communities, and civil society. The Concluding Meeting will take place in Prague on 10-11 September 2026. The conference will be held in person. Registration for the Joint Preparatory Meeting closes on Friday, 28 August 2026. For registration, please contact Ms. Sanavbar Gurukova. https://www.dw.com/en/trump-puts-new-rus.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OLhy It was only days until the US sanctions were to be imposed on Russia Image: Nathan Howard/REUTERS Advertisement US sanctions on Russia will not take effect as planned after President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving them for national security reasons. "I have submitted to the Congress ​a certification that ‌the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the ​United States," ⁠Trump said in the order released by the White House. ​India, one of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, was among the countries that raised concerns about the Russia sanctions bill. The move from the White House comes a week after Trump said the US had agreed to purchase diesel from Russia to try and bring down global energy prices, despite that potentially hurting Ukraine in its war with Russia. The decision was notified on the White House website late in the evening. It noted that the report explaining the decision had been submitted to Congress.
